title: Investor Update — May 2026 (Northpeak Series A)
content:
Investor Update — May 2026
Loomwork, Inc.
To: Northpeak Capital, Board of Directors
From: Maya Chen, CEO
Date: 28 May 2026

Executive Summary
Loomwork continues to make progress in the AI ops copilot space for logistics teams. We closed the Series A with Northpeak in March and have since scaled the team to 12 full-time employees, with a core engineering team of 6 engineers.

Team & Operations
We have grown the team to 12 people. The core engineering team is 6 engineers. We are planning to hire 2 additional Account Executives in Q3 to accelerate the enterprise pipeline.

Financial Position
We closed Q2 with €840,000 in the bank. Monthly burn is approximately €47,000. We have 18 months of runway at current burn. ARR is at €380,000, growing 15% month-over-month.

Pipeline
Enterprise pipeline stands at €1.2M in qualified opportunities. Three deals in final negotiation stage. Largest opportunity is €280,000 ARR with a logistics firm in Rotterdam.

ICP & Strategy
We are moving upmarket. The mid-market self-serve motion remains active but the majority of new qualified pipeline is enterprise. Minimum deal size for new enterprise targets is being raised to €25,000.

title: Board Note — Q2 Runway and Hiring Decision
content:
Board Note — Q2 Runway and Hiring Decision
Prepared by: Devin Park, CTO
Date: 10 June 2026

Runway Clarification
Following the investor update, I want to flag a calculation that needs board attention. The 18-month runway figure in the investor update does not account for the two AE hires planned for Q3. Once those hires go through — assuming start dates in August — we are looking at 9 months of runway, not 18. Each AE is budgeted at €85,000 fully loaded annual cost. This changes our fundraising timeline materially. We need to open a seed extension conversation before end of August.

Hiring Decision
The two AE hires were approved in principle at the last board meeting. Start dates are targeted for August. The fully loaded cost per AE is €85,000 per year including base, commission, and tools.

Action items:
- CEO to initiate conversations with 3 existing investors about bridge or seed extension
- CFO to prepare updated burn model with and without AE hires
- Decision on AE hire timing to be revisited at next board meeting

title: Maya Chen Tweet — June 12 2026
content:
Maya Chen (@mayachen_loomwork) — June 12, 2026

Mid-market teams are the best fit for Loomwork right now. Self-serve onboarding, clear ROI in the first week, and no enterprise procurement cycle. That is where we win.

We are not chasing Fortune 500 logos. We are making ops teams at 50-500 person logistics companies look like heroes.

title: Customer Call — Acme Freight Evaluation
content:
Call Transcript — Acme Freight Evaluation
Date: 3 June 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Loomwork), Jordan Rivera (Acme Freight)

Jordan Rivera: We are evaluating a few tools for our ops team. Our total budget for this category is around €10,000 for the year. Anything above that goes to procurement.

Priya Nair: Understood. Loomwork is priced at €8,000 per year for a team your size.

Jordan Rivera: That fits. We also looked at FreightPilot. They quoted about €6,000 but their onboarding looks heavier. Our ops lead is sceptical.

Priya Nair: FreightPilot is cheaper upfront but the implementation time is longer. Most of our customers switch because of the time-to-value.

Jordan Rivera: Decision authority sits with me for anything under €10,000. I will run the pilot with my team and come back by mid-June.

Priya Nair: Perfect. I will send the pilot terms today.

title: Sales Call — Brightway Logistics
content:
Call Transcript — Brightway Logistics
Date: 14 May 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Loomwork), Ops Director (Brightway Logistics)

Ops Director: We are comparing Loomwork and FreightPilot for our dispatch team. FreightPilot came in about 30% cheaper than your quote.

Priya Nair: Can you share the numbers?

Ops Director: FreightPilot is quoting €5,600 per year. Your quote is €8,000. That is roughly a 30% gap.

Priya Nair: I see. The difference is that our pilot includes setup and training. FreightPilot typically charges extra for implementation.

Ops Director: My budget ceiling is €12,000 for this category, so both fit. But I need to justify the premium to finance.

Priya Nair: I can send a case study from a similar customer that saw payback in 6 weeks.

Ops Director: Please do. I have decision authority for spend under €12,000.

title: Account Review — Delta Logix
content:
Call Transcript — Delta Logix Account Review
Date: 17 June 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Loomwork), Procurement Lead (Delta Logix)

Procurement Lead: We are moving Loomwork to a formal evaluation. Our budget authority threshold is €15,000. Anything below that is approved by my team.

Priya Nair: Our proposed annual contract is €14,000.

Procurement Lead: That is within range. We also have FreightPilot on our approved vendor list. They are pushing hard for the same use case.

Priya Nair: FreightPilot is on your list? That is useful to know. What is their main advantage from your perspective?

Procurement Lead: They are already approved, so legal is faster. But their product is not as tailored to dispatch. We will run both pilots in parallel.

Priya Nair: I will coordinate with your team.

title: Follow-up Call — Synapse Logistics
content:
Call Transcript — Synapse Logistics Follow-up
Date: 24 June 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Loomwork), VP Operations (Synapse Logistics)

VP Operations: We want to move forward but the budget is not unlocked until July cycle. The ceiling for my discretionary approval is €12,000.

Priya Nair: Our quote is €11,500 per year.

VP Operations: That fits. I need sign-off from finance, but anything under €12,000 is usually a formality.

Priya Nair: Great. Can we schedule the pilot kickoff for the first week of July?

VP Operations: Yes. The only other vendor still in the mix is FreightPilot. They are cheaper but less specific to logistics workflows. I think we will go with you if the pilot is clean.

Priya Nair: I will send the pilot agreement today.

title: Investor Update — Q1 2026 (Atlas Ventures)
content:
Investor Update — Q1 2026
Loomwork, Inc.
To: Atlas Ventures, Seed Investors
From: Maya Chen, CEO
Date: 2 April 2026

Q1 Highlights
- Team size: 8 people
- Monthly burn: €38,000
- Cash on hand: €920,000
- Runway: 24 months at current burn
- ARR: €240,000

Product & Market
Our ICP remains mid-market logistics companies in the 50-500 employee range. The self-serve motion is the primary acquisition channel. We are not yet focused on enterprise.

Use of Funds
The seed round is funding product and engineering. We plan to add 2 engineers in Q2 and begin a light sales experiment in Q3.

title: Maya Weekly Note — ICP Decision June 20
content:
Maya Weekly Note — ICP Decision
Date: 20 June 2026
Author: Maya Chen

We have a real ICP drift discussion happening. The team is split.

What I believe:
- The tweet I posted this week is true: mid-market self-serve is where we win today.
- The Northpeak update says we are moving upmarket. That is investor-facing language.
- The minimum deal size for new enterprise targets needs to be €25,000 or we will waste sales cycles.

Decision for next 30 days:
- Keep the self-serve motion as the primary channel.
- Run an enterprise experiment with a €25,000 minimum.
- Do not reposition the entire company until we have 3 enterprise closes.

Open question: are we actually moving upmarket, or are we just trying to sound like we are?

title: Pipeline Update — Priya Nair June 25
content:
From: Priya Nair
To: Maya Chen, Devin Park
Date: 25 June 2026
Subject: Pipeline Update — 4 deals, 3 blocked by budget authority

Hi team,

Quick pipeline update. We have 4 active evaluation deals. Three are blocked by budget authority thresholds:

1. Acme Freight — €8,000 quote. Buyer has authority up to €10,000. Moving to pilot.
2. Brightway Logistics — €8,000 quote. Buyer has authority up to €12,000. Waiting on case study.
3. Delta Logix — €14,000 quote. Buyer has authority up to €15,000. Approved vendor list includes FreightPilot.
4. Synapse Logistics — €11,500 quote. Buyer has authority up to €12,000. Budget unlocks in July.

Pattern: budget authority is the blocker in 3 out of 4 deals. None of the deals exceed the buyer's ceiling, but the approval process is still adding friction. FreightPilot is mentioned in every deal as the cheaper alternative.

Next step: I will consolidate the objections and draft a one-page budget authority battlecard.

Priya

title: Lost Deal Debrief — FreightMax Nordic
content:
Lost Deal Debrief — FreightMax Nordic
Date: 19 June 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Loomwork), Former Champion (FreightMax Nordic)

Former Champion: I wanted to give you honest feedback. We went with FreightPilot.

Priya Nair: I appreciate that. What was the deciding factor?

Former Champion: Price. FreightPilot was €30,000 cheaper over three years. That was the entire conversation in procurement.

Priya Nair: €30,000 cheaper? That is a large gap.

Former Champion: They have a Nordics-specific bundle. Your product is better for our workflows but I could not defend the premium to finance.

Priya Nair: Was there anything we could have done differently?

Former Champion: A clearer ROI case and a budget authority note. Our buyer's threshold was €15,000 and your three-year quote was well above it.

Priya Nair: Thank you. This is very helpful.

title: Sam Vora Email — Runway and ICP Alignment
content:
From: Sam Vora
To: Maya Chen
Date: 13 June 2026
Subject: Runway and ICP Alignment

Hi Maya,

Quick note after reading the May investor update and your tweet this week.

Runway: The 18-month figure is helpful but I want to make sure it is net of the AE hires. If the board note is right, the real number is closer to 9 months. I would not present the 18-month figure to new investors without the AE caveat.

ICP: The update says upmarket, the tweet says mid-market. These are not the same. I can defend either strategy to a lead, but I need you to pick one in the next update.

Happy to jump on a call.

Sam
